cursor:ACC-02.answer: Users choose among many models from several providers inside Cursor's own agent harness; hosting third-party agent harnesses is not documented in the pages read.

cursor:ACC-03.answer: Access uses a Cursor account and Cursor subscription with usage pools; own provider API keys work for chat models only.

cursor:ACC-04.answer: Cloud Agents need a paid plan and connected source control (or a no-repo start); setup is agent-led or Dockerfile-based; self-managed machines attach through the CLI worker.

cursor:ACC-05.answer: Cursor exposes a CLI with headless mode, a public-beta Cloud Agents REST API, a TypeScript SDK, and signed status webhooks on the legacy API.

cursor:ACC-06.answer: Cursor is an MCP client with OAuth and admin allowlists, supports plugins and marketplaces, and reads skills, subagents and hooks from other tools' folders.

cursor:PLAN-02.answer: Plan Mode produces editable markdown plans before building; acceptance criteria, revision history and plan-to-work links are not documented.

cursor:PLAN-03.answer: Projects let a coordinator agent plan larger bodies of work and delegate to cloud agents; task dependencies, readiness and blockers are not described.

cursor:PLAN-04.answer: Rules, AGENTS.md, skills, team rules, automation memories and Project shared-context files carry instructions and knowledge across sessions.

cursor:PLAN-05.answer: Agents search code with a local grep index, web search and MCP, and accept image inputs; embeddings-based indexing, citations and conflict detection are not documented.

cursor:PLAN-07.answer: Agents interact with external Linear and Jira issues (assigned or mentioned) and report progress there; a native agent-readable issue store was not found.

cursor:COORD-01.answer: Many agents can run in parallel across local worktrees, remote machines and the cloud; no numeric cloud concurrency limit is stated.

cursor:COORD-02.answer: Work is routed to repos, environments and pools by rules and mentions; ownership is the creating user, with follow-ups governed by a team setting.

cursor:COORD-03.answer: Subagents (built-in and custom) and Project coordinators delegate work with isolated context and return final summaries; they can be resumed by ID.

cursor:COORD-04.answer: Automations run on schedules, source-control events, Slack, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty and webhooks; Projects can subscribe to PRs, CI and schedules.

cursor:COORD-05.answer: Users can steer, queue, cancel, resume and follow agents from several clients; notifications reach mobile and Slack.

cursor:COORD-06.answer: The Agents Window and mobile inbox list agents and Projects show coordinator-managed agents; dependency and workload views were not found.

cursor:COORD-07.answer: Cursor supports quick one-off tasks, longer coordinator-led Projects, custom modes and subagent definitions; in-run changes are limited to steering.

cursor:RUN-02.answer: Local agents use worktrees and an OS sandbox; cloud agents run in per-agent Firecracker microVMs with configurable network egress and redacted secrets.

cursor:RUN-03.answer: Cloud runs survive client disconnects and can be resumed; workspaces are recycled after idle and snapshots expire after 90 days of inactivity.
